Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 3. Otesaconazole, a BCRP inhibitor, may enhance the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates. Consider using the lowest starting dose of the BCRP substrate or reducing its dose. 4. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. When pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates, increase monitoring for drug-related adverse effects. 8. Resmetirom increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Resmetirom, a weak CYP2C8 inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. 10. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 11. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 12. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 13. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 16. Voxilaprevir increases the levels of seladelpar through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Monitor seladelpar for adverse effects when coadministered with BCRP inhibitors. 18. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 19. Administer drugs with pH-dependent solubility at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 20. Voxilaprevir increases the levels or effects of selexipag through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Selexipag is a substrate of ABCG2 (BCRP). Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when coadministered with ABCG2 (BCRP) inhibitors. 22. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing hepatic CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Sparsentan, a CYP2B6 inducer, reduces the exposure and efficacy of CYP2B6 substrates. 24. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 25. Stiripentol increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Stiripentol is a BCRP transport inhibitor and may increase the levels or effects of BCRP substrates. 27. Stiripentol is a CYP2C8 inhibitor and may increase the levels or effects of CYP2C8 substrates. 28. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 29. Stiripentol is a CYP2B6 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 30. Tafamidis increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir through mechanisms other than direct enzymatic inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tafamidis inhibits breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) in vitro and may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Dosage adjustments of these substrates may be necessary. 32. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. 34. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer.
